title: External products for cone unstraightening
statement:
Use the coherent realization, small simplicial categories, enriched diagrams, cone adjunction $L_\phi\dashv U_\phi$, and its simplexwise definition from [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. Let $S,S'$ be small simplicial sets, $D,D'$ small simplicial categories, $\phi:\mathfrak C[S]\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\phi':\mathfrak C[S']\to(D')^{\mathrm{op}}$ simplicial functors, and $F:D\to\mathrm{sSet}$ and $G:D'\to\mathrm{sSet}$ simplicial functors. Define $(F\boxtimes G)(d,d')=F(d)\times G(d')$, with product action. Let $\phi\boxtimes\phi'$ be the composite from $\mathfrak C[S\times S']$ to $D^{\mathrm{op}}\times(D')^{\mathrm{op}}=(D\times D')^{\mathrm{op}}$ obtained by the two projections of $S\times S'$ followed by $\phi$ and $\phi'$. Then the maps to the two factors induce a natural simplicial isomorphism over $S\times S'$,
$$U_{\phi\boxtimes\phi'}(F\boxtimes G)\cong U_\phi(F)\times U_{\phi'}(G).$$
These isomorphisms commute with maps of diagrams and with the canonical associativity and unit identifications for products. In particular let $S'=\Delta^0$, let $D'$ be the terminal simplicial category and $\phi'$ its canonical isomorphism, and let $G$ have value a simplicial set $K$. Then, writing $F\times K$ for the objectwise product diagram, there is a natural isomorphism
$$U_\phi(F\times K)\cong U_\phi(F)\times\operatorname{Sing}_Q K$$
over $S$, compatible with iterated products and the terminal simplicial set. Here $Q^n=\mathfrak C[(\Delta^n\star\{y\})\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}](x,y)$ and $(\operatorname{Sing}_Q K)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^n,K)$, as in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. No fibrancy assumption on $F,G,K$ or on the bases is made; all constructions are small in a universe containing the displayed inputs.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.12, printed p.78, external-product isomorphism and its specialization to the point Read online; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this simplicial model-category fact.

proof.text:
For a diagram $F:D\to\mathrm{sSet}$ form the simplicial category $E_F$ with objects $\operatorname{Ob}(D^{\mathrm{op}})\amalg\{v\}$, with its old mapping objects those of $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, and with
$$E_F(d,v)=F(d),\qquad E_F(v,d)=\varnothing,\qquad E_F(v,v)=\Delta^0.$$
For $r:d\to e$ in $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, composition $E_F(e,v)\times D^{\mathrm{op}}(d,e)\to E_F(d,v)$ is the action of $F$ on $r^{\mathrm{op}}$. Associativity and the identity laws are exactly the action laws of the enriched functor $F$; all other new compositions involve an identity or an empty mapping object. Thus this is a real small simplicial category, with no fibrancy requirement.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, correspondence interpretation of straightening; explicit auxiliary construction for Remark 2.2.2.12

proof.text:
Fix $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$. Write $A=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, $B=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n\star\Delta^0]$, $a=\phi\mathfrak C[\sigma]:A\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $T_i=B(i,v)$ for $0\leq i\leq n$. The explicit coherent-simplex definition in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] shows that $A$ is the full initial subcategory of $B$, that $B(v,i)=\varnothing$, and that $B(v,v)=\Delta^0$. Define a diagram $R:D\to\mathrm{sSet}$ by the following degreewise quotient:
$$R(d)=\left(\coprod_{i=0}^n D^{\mathrm{op}}(d,a(i))\times T_i\right)/\sim,\qquad [a(h)\circ r,t]_j=[r,t\circ h]_i.$$
Here in each simplicial degree $h\in A(i,j)$, $r\in D^{\mathrm{op}}(d,a(i))$ and $t\in T_j$; the equivalence relation is generated by these pairs. Simplicial operators preserve the relation because composition and $a$ are simplicial maps. Precomposition on $r$ defines the $D$-action and respects the relation by associativity.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, the cone pushout; explicit degreewise presentation of its mixed mapping objects

proof.text:
Apply the construction of step 1 to $R$, giving $E_R$. There are functors $D^{\mathrm{op}}\to E_R$ and $B\to E_R$, agreeing on $A$; the latter sends $t\in T_i$ to $[1_{a(i)},t]$. They exhibit $E_R$ as the pushout $B\amalg_A D^{\mathrm{op}}$. Indeed, for any simplicial category $Z$, compatible functors $H:D^{\mathrm{op}}\to Z$ and $J:B\to Z$ uniquely extend: on a mixed mapping object the extension is
$$[r,t]\longmapsto J(t)\circ H(r).$$
The defining relation is respected since $H(a(h))=J(h)$ and composition in $Z$ is associative. The map respects precomposition, and hence composition; uniqueness follows from $[r,t]=[1_{a(i)},t]\circ r$. This verifies the pushout universal property rather than assuming a theorem on enriched Kan extensions. Consequently $R(d)$ identifies with $M_{\sigma,\phi}(d,v)=L_\phi(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)(d)$ of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen].

source.place: Section 2.2.1, displayed definition of the cone pushout; universal-property verification

proof.text:
Under step 3, an enriched natural transformation $\alpha:L_\phi(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)\to F$ is equivalent to a functor $M_{\sigma,\phi}\to E_F$ which is the identity on $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and sends the cone vertex to $v$: its maps on the mixed mapping objects are the $\alpha_d$, and its composition equations there are exactly the action-square equalities. By the pushout universal property this is equivalently a functor
$$b:\mathfrak C[\Delta^n\star\Delta^0]\to E_F,\qquad b|_A=\phi\mathfrak C[\sigma],\quad b(v)=v.$$
Both directions are restriction or the unique pushout extension, so they are inverse. By the simplex formula in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen], these are precisely the $n$-simplices of $U_\phi F$ above $\sigma$.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, simplexwise right adjoint of cone straightening; expansion used in Remark 2.2.2.12

proof.text: For a simplex $\tau=(\sigma,\sigma'):\Delta^n\to S\times S'$, the full subcategory of $E_F\times E_G$ on the objects $(d,d')$ and $(v,v')$ is canonically $E_{F\boxtimes G}$: its old mapping objects are those of $(D\times D')^{\mathrm{op}}$, its mixed mapping objects are $F(d)\times G(d')$, its outgoing mapping objects at $(v,v')$ are empty, and its endomorphism object there is terminal. A pair of cone functors $b,b'$ of step 4 pairs to a functor into this full subcategory, since its initial objects are $(\phi\sigma(i),\phi'\sigma'(i))$ and its last object is $(v,v')$. Conversely the two projections recover $b,b'$. Composition and the prescribed restriction to $A$ hold coordinatewise, and pairing and projection are mutually inverse. Thus step 4 gives the required bijection on $n$-simplices above each $\tau$.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.12, first displayed external-product isomorphism; explicit simplexwise inverse

proof.text: For a simplex operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, restriction in step 4 is precomposition with $\mathfrak C[\theta\star1_{\Delta^0}]$; its initial restriction is the prescribed map for $\sigma\theta$. The product bijection of step 5 commutes with it because $(b,b')\mathfrak C[\theta\star1]=(b\mathfrak C[\theta\star1],b'\mathfrak C[\theta\star1])$. A map of diagrams $\alpha:F\to\widetilde F$ induces a functor $E_F\to E_{\widetilde F}$, identity on old objects and mapping objects and equal to $\alpha_d$ on $E_F(d,v)$. Postcomposition by this functor commutes with pairing, and likewise for $G$. Therefore the bijections and their inverses are simplicial and natural in the diagrams. They preserve $(\sigma,\sigma')$, so give an isomorphism over $S\times S'$, with forward map the two canonical projections.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.12, naturality of the first displayed isomorphism; simplex-operator check

proof.text: For three factors both iterated applications of step 5 send a triple of cone functors to $(b_1,b_2,b_3)$, with the two bracketings related by the canonical product associator on objects and mapping objects. Every cone into the one-object terminal simplicial category is unique. Its unstraightening over $\Delta^0$ has exactly one simplex in each degree, by the simplex formula. Hence adding this factor leaves $b$ unchanged under the product unitor. These coordinatewise descriptions prove associativity and unit compatibility; iterating pairing gives the same coordinate list for any number of factors.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.12, canonical product isomorphism; explicit associativity and unit checks

proof.text:
Specialize to $S'=\Delta^0$ and the terminal simplicial category $D'$. The fiber formula in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen], which holds for every diagram, identifies $U_{\phi'}G$ with $\operatorname{Sing}_Q K$; its whole base is the point. This uses exactly the $Q^n$ defined in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Step 5 therefore gives $U_\phi(F\times K)\cong U_\phi(F)\times\operatorname{Sing}_QK$ over $S$. Finally, the bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^n,K\times L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^n,K)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^n,L)$$
are pairing and projection, commute with precomposition by every $Q(\theta)$, and send the unique map to the terminal simplicial set to the unique pair. Together with step 7 this proves all iterated-product and terminal compatibilities in the specialization. None of these arguments uses Kan conditions; the finite coproducts and degreewise quotients in steps 1--3 remain in a universe containing the inputs.
